text:
sqlpipe is a command-line tool for moving data out of Postgres and into S3, one table at a time. Point it at a database and a bucket, and it reads your tables, converts each one into columnar Parquet files, and uploads them to the object store you specify. It handles both full snapshots and incremental syncs, so you can keep a low-cost, query-ready copy of your operational data in S3 without standing up a heavyweight ETL platform.

Built for analytics and archival workflows, sqlpipe produces Parquet that plugs straight into engines like Athena, Trino, DuckDB, and Spark. Runs are configuration-driven and idempotent, making them easy to schedule with cron or your orchestrator of choice. Whether you're offloading historical rows, feeding a data lake, or building a durable backup, sqlpipe keeps the path from Postgres to S3 simple, fast, and repeatable.
